messages:
Samir K.: quick sync — ACME asked for per-customer fallback rules that prefer lower-cost quantized variants for EU traffic only. need to scope PRD + acceptance criteria. who wants ownership?
Alana P.: I can draft PRD scope. couple questions: is this purely routing rules (policy) or do we need telemetry changes to show per-customer fallback economics?
Joanne (Prod): Both. Sales wants cost delta surfaced per request and a dashboard for customers to opt into/opt-out of cost fallbacks. also need contractual opt-in for EU data residency.
Kevin (Eng Runtime): runtime impact: we need compatibility checks for model variants at route time. naive plan: maintain a "compatibility map" and reject fallbacks if kv-cache ABI differs.
Matt (SRE): ops concerns: if EU pool calls cheaper variants, latency tail might change. we need SLO experiments and canary rollout plan (region + customer subset).
Samir K.: Alana — include acceptance criteria: 1) policy language to express region + customer rules, 2) telemetry + billing markers, 3) compatibility guard that prevents silent corruption, 4) rollout gates and SLA rollback.
Alana P.: drafting now. putting a minimal policy DSL example in PRD. feedback?
Joanne (Prod): include an explicit customer-facing revert path and notification flow. sales needs an API to toggle per-account fallback.
Kevin (Eng Runtime): sketch of compatibility map (will add to PRD):
```
# model compatibility (example)
base:model-a-1.0 -> fallbacks: [model-a-1.0-q4, model-a-1.0-q8]
constraints: kv-cache-format==v2, max-seq=2048
region-compat: { eu: true, us-west: true, apac: false }
```

Kevin (Eng Runtime): runtime will validate constraints at routing time and fall back to next compatible variant when allowed by policy. if none compatible, use primary route or fail open?
Joanne (Prod): fail open only if customer-level policy allows degradation. default should be fail closed (no silent variant swap).
Matt (SRE): rollout plan suggestion:
- canary 5% EU traffic for internal test accounts
- monitor p99 latency, token cost delta, correctness signals for 48h
- expand to 25% then 100% if thresholds OK
add automatic rollback if p99 increases >15% or correctness alerts fire.
Samir K.: acceptance criteria (proposal):
- Policy DSL implemented and validated in staging (unit tests + policy fuzzing)
- Telemetry emits `fallback_applied=true|false` and `fallback_variant` per request
- Billing metadata attached to tokens to compute customer-level savings report
- Compatibility map prevents fallback if ABI mismatch; failing that, route to primary
- Canary rollout + automatic rollback metrics in Console
Alana P.: will add customer opt-in API and product copy for support docs. also capture edge case: mixed-session fallback (first tokens on primary, subsequent tokens on fallback) — need KV-cache rewarm strategy.
Kevin (Eng Runtime): edge-case notes: mixing variants mid-session -> KV cache invalidation. options: 1) disallow session switch, 2) warm cache via prefix-copy (expensive), 3) accept warmup latency. PRD should pick default: disallow mid-session switch unless explicit migration API used.
Joanne (Prod): agree on disallowing mid-session switch for GA. track requests that attempted switch as telemetry.
Matt (SRE): add runbook for incidents: detect sudden spike in fallback_applied + p50->p99 divergence -> circuit-break region-level fallback.
routing-bot: automations: created ticket INF-4821 and PRD draft link: https://redwood.internal/notes/INF-4821 (Alana please attach compatibility matrix) :robot_face:
Samir K.: thanks — Alana will share first PRD draft by EOD. volunteers for tech review? Kevin + Matt can pair on runtime/ops sections. Joanne will handle product + legal hooks.
Alana P.: noted. will ping for review once draft up. :thumbsup:
